To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cloud properties retrieved from SEVIRI data are in reasonable agreement with the input truth.

the APICS cloud property retrieval is able to retrieve realistic cloud properties from simulated SEVIRI radiances, that the CMSAF cloud property retrieval is not yet able to do so, that the retrieval of cloud top height is more difficult than the retrieval of cloud phase and that cloud optical properties and cloud water path are most difficult to retrieve.
the cloud property retrievals of the DLR Institute of Atmospheric Physics and of the CMSAF of EUMETSAS perform well in terms of detection and cloud phase discrimination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of cloud property retrievs from passive space borne imagers.
the validation and improvement of satellite cloud property retrieval algorithms by using realistic cloud structures from the COSMO-Eu weather forecast model.
the validation of cloud retrievals with the help of realistic simulations of satellite radiances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

both retrieval algorithms are capable to reproduce cloud properties at a spatial scale relevant for satellite observations, but that there is still room for improvements, especially for the retrieval of cloud effective radii.
both algorithms perform well, but APICS shows a slightly better performance in the case of water clouds and CMSAF for ice clouds.
both retrieval algorithms perform well, with the DLR algorithm being slightly better.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DLR algorithm performs better for cloud phase and cloud top temperature while CMSAF has the advantage for cloud optical thickness and cloud water path.
cloud properties retrieved from simulated SEVIRI radiances are in good agreement with the input "truth" and that the APICS code is a good starting point for further development.
the DLR algorithm shows a better performance than the CMSAF retrieval in most cases, but the latter has a better performance in the case of ice clouds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the validation of cloud property retrievs from satellite observations can be improved by realistic simulations of the radiance observations, which can be obtained with a combination of high resolution weather model data, statistical downscaling, and a one-dimensional radiative tranfer model.
the proposed validation approach is a valuable and promising tool for the evaluation of satellite cloud property retrieval algorithms.
the proposed approach is very valuable in order to validate cloud property retrievals.
